What's worse, some players have the ability to change Pokemon at will during battles, giving them an advantage hard to beat. When I see they have this ability, I highly tail it out of the battle There are around a thousand different Pokemon and they never seem to show up so feel that catching them all ia impossible . Sometime it can take over ten balls to catch, very monotonous!

Went to use PokeCoins to buy one of the box sets and when I saw the next day that none of the items from said box were there, I contacted Support. Was refused my rightful refund because I had inadvertently used items from the other box in the meantime. So I basically got screwed over because I didn't catch their mistake until it was too late. Real dick move, Niantic.

I've started playing 7/7/16. I've played literally every day since. You will always see people complaining about the game, myself included, but we all keep playing anyway. The amount of things to do is enormous, although it can become stale, especially for veteran players like me. I've walked hundreds of miles, made dozens of new friends and made many great memories playing this game. PoGo will always be special to me.

Even though the wifi sometimes works, it's really good and gets me walking and outside. A lot of the reviews are just "Oh, it ruins my posture!" But, if you move your phone closer to your face, your posture will be fine, just get into that habit. This game is fun to play but I do wish that the CP could be much higher for de-evelutions like Eevee and Pikachu and whatever. I truly, honestly recommend this app. Give it a chance at least

This game used too be a lot of fun. But the reason for the change of the review is the constant updating. With constant updates the games starting to lag and will even crash. Not too mention it's slowly becoming a P2P game.. atleast that's what it seems like and I've heard others say that as well. I used to really enjoy this game but now it just feels like they're not putting much effort in anymore...

I've been playing since it released... I have consistently mixed feelings about it. Some items are impossible to get (impossible literally and or as to take so long as to seem impossible and pointless), can't advance certain missions for such long periods it's frustrating enough to take extended breaks. Worst, if you're not in a city center, you have nowhere near enough stops and gyms. Suburban areas should have MORE. We can't just walk everywhere. It's not even safe.

I have been playing this game since October of 2016. I cringe every time you release an update. I play it to relax and unwind during my off time. I have found that due to crashes and failures to load, I am MORE stressed due to this game. The memory requirements are now so burdensome that I can barely enjoy playing on a good day. Thanks for ruining the only game I have ever enjoyed playing on my phone. Considered releasing a version with LESS graphic requirements, so I can play without crashes.

If you're looking to catch 'mons and send them to Home, this app works fine. If you're looking at this like it's a standalone game, don't. Battles are unbalanced, especially regarding online PvP. This game has no servers for the player battles, they are Peer-2-Peer, so lagswitching is rampant. The Raids are for lots of people, you won't even beat a 3-star on your own, even halfway to max level, and 5-stars need TWENTY people. This game could still be decent, but the battles need an overhaul.

My family is very out doorsey and this just gives us something else to do together. Hope the battle systems get better though. Would like to see attacks like confusion and poison actually do something during the battle and poison maybe outside the battle too, until an antidote is used. Overall a fun game. Love seeing the looks on my kids face when they see the rare they want in the wild, or the hard work of evolving.

Constantly having me update the app once a week at least. Wants me to delete other games to continue playing. Tired of always having to update. Updated 4 times this month alone! I used to love playing the game. But I can leave the game with 195 balls, only to open it the next day and have NO balls.. how is that?? I've just deleted the game again.

New update erased my teams, removed the ability to paste into the name field, can't place the cursor in the name field (must delete from end to error point) and now it powers down my screen. The new defender/streak functionality is nice but I'd give it back in a heartbeat for the ability to manipulate the name text as it used to be. Not well thought out.

You're going to have a hard time playing this game if you live in a rural area like myself. Pokemon spawns are few and far apart out here, so if you want to catch a lot of Pokemon in a short amount of time, your best bet is driving to your nearest town or buying incense to increase spawn rates. Overall it's a great fun little app to collect all your favorite Pokemon.

The game can be a lot of fun, but please do not give this company your money! Niantic will try to lure you into buying event tickets and other items, but in the end the players always get scammed into buying something that doesn't live up to the hype. Playing the game without buying stuff is absolutely possible, and the less people buy the more the company will realize we won't take being scammed anymore. GO Fest 2022 was a joke.

I have been playing since the game first came out. And I used to give this game a 4 star, because of a few bugs that need addressed. Today I am here to give it a 1 star. There are so many issues with this game anymore, it is unbelievable. Just read the reviews to see for yourself. Niantic does not seem to care about us players or fixing issues that cost us money. I lost faith in you Niantic, this game has so much potential.

After coming back to the game after years of not playing. It has for sure improved. Now in my opinion it hasn't improved enough in the 4 plus years it's been out. If feels almost as if nothing has changed. The worst the game has to offer is the fact that it takes so long to hear any feedback from the Developers. I'm glad they took steps and hopefully I will rewrite this review in the future once I see better communication.

Been playing since the beginning and it has gotten less fun and more tedious after peaking a couple years ago. The Battle Game is still decent but the rest is more simplistic grind than fun gaming experience. Paid events are frequently problematic or disappointing. If you love Pokemon and live in a city or suburb it is still worthwhile. If not, probably better off playing something else.

It's still a work in progress in the same way most mobile games are, but it's a solid Pokemon game. Considering how many mobile games I've played for hours and not enjoyed a second of, having even just the handful of minutes I got the first day be instantly fun was worth it. Since the recent updates, I've even got hours of fun out of this game! Plus, servers have been running smooth for quite a while now. Seeing as it continues going uphill, I will give a higher rating for this amazing game.

When I have 8 gifts, and my buddy brings me 10, why do I still only have 8 gifts? Also. my friends list won't sort properly. It shows me a few that have sent me gifts, then goes to alphabetical order, then there are other gift friend mixed in, and when I view a friend then return to the list, it jumps around and I have to scroll back to where I was.

It has really grown. I prefer console in a lot of ways, but it's just about all I could've asked for. Maybe add it where friends showed up on the map with you? Have an option for that? My phone can't stop freezing now.. October 27, 2019 my phone can no longer handle this game, I've had a blast, but I'm uninstalling until I can get a decent phone

Niantic got too greedy and ruined the game. Four years ago I said I wouldn't play this game. When I met my now fiance she got me hooked on it. I didn't spend as much as some but I at least forked out $200 over the course of three years trickling down to a few dollars here and there for events. Recent changes have destroyed this game due to Niantics' greed. I hate greed! No more $$$ Niantic! 😡

They fix something they break something. This game will never be fully functional to play in its entirety considering whenever they released new content something breaks and features that should be there are not. Here, play our game, wait you can't because we've introduced another issue that makes it difficult if not impossible for you to do so. Please test in a sandbox environment before you release updates, thanks. Other than that, I'll continue to play because I love Pokemon.

Updated to one star on 4-9-23. Time to step up and answer to your players. Consumers are spending money and time on a game they enjoy. With that said if you're turning a profit, its probably time to fix issues that are very well known. I enjoy the game, but sometimes I can't even get past the initial loading screen. It's crazy, I can pay for a remote raid pass and the transaction goes through flawlessly, but attempting to join a raid is a hit or miss and I will lose my pass.

I've always been a Pokemon fan. This game just excites my love for it even more!!! There are sometimes a few bugs and it would be nice if we could just give items/pokemon to friends instead of having to trade them or send them a surprise gift. And I personally feel like the bag and storage upgrades cost a bit too much. But other than these, it is a really fun game and I would recommend it to anyone in the Pokémon fandom whether they're brand new or have been here for a while!

I love the idea behind this app, but lets face it, it's mostly just a money grab. It's impossible for many people in rural areas to keep up and forget trying to catch legendaries if the game isn't popular in your area. this game wasn't made for anyone with a real life to tend to... and yet those are the ones capable of dumping money into the game to fund it. I'll keep the app, but I barely use it anymore. sadly...

The game can be fun, but definitely favors those who pay real money, or have been playing daily since the beginning. As someone who lives in a rural area, the recent changes to remote raids have made it even more difficult to catch up and compete. Until Niantic solves these issues, and stops showing favoritism to those who live in big cities, I cannot recommend this game.

I rate it two cause one, the trading system kinda lessens the way original pokemon is played out cause your friend(s) have to be so close to each other, but when you add people from different states or countries you don't need to be that close and I kinda want that feature to be changed cause it seems pointless to trade from a lot of friends you know around the world. also two, dont make it where you can't trade back, that's kinda dumb if you ask me. I'll rate it better when this is fixed.

Great game overall, but the latest update crashed it! I've had multiple instances of opening to a frozen screen and have had to uninstall and reinstall the game to get it to work... for a little bit. Or the game goes from the Niantic loading screen to just a black screen, and nothing happens. The avatar updates are also very disappointing

I've recently re- downloaded this game, and they've made a ton of improvements, my only issue these days is that 90% of encounters with previously undiscovered pokemon results in the target fleeing. It also seems like every time I have over 20 pokeballs pokemon will keep escaping, forcing me to use 8-12 balls, and then just running away. It's really frustrating how often that happens since there's no way to prevent them from escaping.

Frustrating the number of times I am unable to find a raid party, not enough local players and when you do find a raid you end up not catching the Pokemon after freezing your butt off, just lost any value in playing it. Is fun for a month and then it gets boring. At least Monster hunters AR game let's you mark monsters while you walk so you can battle them later, would be nice to have something like that. I guess Lures are kind of like that.

thanks guys, played for a long time and had fun. now, out of nowhere without notification, my phone is "incompatible with this app." would have been nice for a quick heads up that phones with 32-bit were being phased out of your game. otherwise, you lost a bunch of customers and players without letting us know. in a game that gives out details constantly, you'd think that this would have been an important one. we shouldn't have to dive into the internet to find out why a day after playing 🙄

After a four year break I returned to Pokemon Go. They certainly solved the issue it use to have of lacking content. Now you can battle, catch multiple generation of pokemon, trade, ect ect it'd great BUT! Now the issue is the app itself (can't have your cake and eat it too). Now I have pokemon that don't show up in my roster. I get kicked out of raids. Mega evolved pokemon disappear and support refuses to reimburse me. It's just a mess! Nothing ruins immersion like a poorly maintained app.

The Developers Don't Listen to their Players. I love the game but can't respect the blatant disregard for the greater player bases desires going unheard and unacknowledged by the developers. If you're playing to have fun, the novelty can wear off quickly without others around. If you play in a rural area, they have made a point to not make the game for you which is sad to see. I'd only recommend this game if you've already invested 1+ years into it.

I know this app is still new and seriously addictive! I'm having issues with pokémon that spawn, but are not loading (I'm seeing the white circles but not the pokémon) and I'm constantly having to force stop and reload the game. I'm attempting a reinstall to see if it fixes the issue and I have reported the issue. Hopefully this will stop happening, because it affects captures and being able to fight in gyms as well, I'm not giving up on the game yet! UPDATE: 2/13/19 STILL PLAYING!

The game itself cool, the support non existent. Prior raid had issues and submitted help request and was told to do it sooner, had similar issue and did it immediately following the raid and was told "after thorough investigation" I was allowed to raid. I was not, my last pokemon never appeared and I was unable to get a new battle party and rejoin because it was stuck on an invisible fainted pokemon. We shouldn't have to purchase extra revives because the game wasn't correctly working.

I would raise my rating to 5* if and only if they buffed remote raids again. There are not enough gyms near me, and often I don't have time to go to the few that are. Make them less pricey, or at least raise the limit of how many you can do. PLEASE NIANTIC! Also, the news doesn't come until two or three days after the game says they do. I check one day, and the next day I have news that says 2 days ago. Fix it!

I love everything about it except that in my area there are ZERO pokestops and nowhere to raid. We have two schools nearby and I thought maybe one would be a pokestop, but there is absolutely nothing until you get to the next town. This is frustrating because I run out of pokeballs extremely fast and can not go get more from pokestops. My friends level up way faster than me from this.

I spent around $40 for coins for remote raiding before they announced their price hikes. I feel like I wasted money and will not be getting the value I paid for. I used the app a lot for walks, but remote raiding was my favorite add-on at night before bed. $2 for a CHANCE to catch a digital creature is outrageous. I am uninstalling off my phone, but I wish I could also get my money back because the game is no longer worth it; it's no longer fun, just frustrating.

This game was buggy enough when you just were trying to catch Pokemon, now that you guys introduced your buggy raid system it is approaching unplayable. I've worked hard to reach level 32 but I'm done playing until I hear that you guys worked out some of these issues. I played Ingress from beta and even in beta it still had ten times the playabity. update have picked it back up after this long and it has gotten better so it restored my faith in letting players decide for themselves.

Very fun and addictive game! The game adopts the essentials of Pokémon in a tap based format as well incorporating "catching" creatures by "throwing" a pokeball versus previous Pokémon formats. The game does not incorporate "all" the features veteran Pokémon players know and love. Battling and trading format is significantly different than previous games. Creatures and "Movesets" lack the special abilities that other games incorporate. Regardless, i recommend all Pokémon fans to play this game!

Niantic suspended my account because I had Shazam installed on my phone and they flagged it as a third party app. I could not get in touch with a person to help resolve this, only automated messages. I had to delete Shazam to play again. Update: 2 months later and no change to the apps on my phone, and I get an account termination notice out of nowhere. I'm just not interested in anything Niantic does from this point on. I'd recommend not playing their games, they don't deserve it.

Originally rated this game 4 stars and thought it was pretty good. Until I realized you can be locked out of your account and lose LITERAL YEARS of progress for simply updating the app. I looked further into it and found that others have gone through the same thing, often never getting back into their original accounts. I've had my account since 2017. To lock me out and say I can't be "authenticated" with the same information I've been using for 5 years is ludicrous. Don't download.

I love that I can walk with my favorite Pokemon to collect the candy I need for evolutions. But I DO with they could integrate the purchase of berries and hard to get stones with poke coins. Sometimes I am not in an area bwith a lot of pokestops and gyms and without a car it is very difficult to get to certain places to even catch rare Pokemon. By after almost 3 years, I STILL play several times a day usually.. lol-edit- after 3 years, it's still the same.

I first started in 2021, but stopped after 2ish weeks because there was only one pokestop in my town. July 2023, I picked it up again since I had to walk around mile a day anyway to get to my classes. Recently, I noticed that the app has been buggy, but since yesterday, I can't play the game. Every time I hop in the game, it loads everything, then crashes once the announcements appear. Today is day 2 of this happening. Please fix this problem so I can keep playing it on my android.

We've all surely fell victim to crashes mid catch. Or, walking twice the distance to hatch an egg. Hell, it seems like every other level I don't receive loot for leveling up! I love this game but I feel like some of us deserve a gift for sticking it out through the tough bugs. Just a thought Edit #3: support is not supportive. They really don't care about the players. Considering uninstalling

Not gonna lie this is a good game i like it but it's not for everyone there are those who have their common sense to know that this is a work in progress and there are those who have the attention span too that of a 3 year old. Good game i haven't had any problem with it yea there are server updated that prevent you from logging in but they tend to last 1-2 hours tops. All the other features will come along.

I used to love this game. It was nice to have the option of either remote or in-person raids. The events and community days were much better, too. However, with the recent price increases and declining event quality, I can no longer raid remotely as often and I don't have as much fun playing overall. It has become resoundingly clear that Niantic values profit over players.

NOT free to play. It's fun and free for a little while but, there is no way to replenish your pokieballs when you run out.... EXCEPT by paying actual money for gold coins, and then using the coins to purchase pokie balls. I love how they tell us how many times this was downloaded, but NO mention of how many times it was UNINSTALLED. I gave two stars because, it was fun while it was free. Now I will be removing it from my phone.

I do not recommend anything Niantic. My kid hasn't played on his account in years. The email associated with the account was deleted due to inactivity. Customer service was not helpful. The verification questions had to do with events in the game and coin balance..... my kid can't remember where he put his socks 5 minutes ago. Didn't ask for our names or anything like that. Don't invest in them. Their solution is to make a new account and restart.

Good game. Been playing since it came out with my dad--who initially knew pretty much zilch about Pokémon (he now plays more than me). Does tend to crash for me but it might just be my phone's fault. ☆ I wish there was a chat feature that had preset messages for friends (help set up raids or trades). ☆ It would also be nice to be able to friend people when you join a gym.

The update to the character model is so ugly that I can't stand looking at my character and play the game. He looks like a hunchback ogre and it completely ruins the experience. That's after trying the character customization to the "best" available settings. I'm not sinking another penny or minute into this game until the character models are fixed.

Played it on my friends phone. It's a good game, but they need to get full tablet support and support for similar devices. They're really missing out on a higher rating because of this, tbh. Most people with tablets aren't able to get past the character creation screen and it will crash when it tries to load up. So, if you're part of the unlucky group that only owns a tablet, we're going to have to sit and wait around for it to get support.

Remote raid passes basically doubled in price. Okay... it's not even a guaranteed catch. It's hard to get people to play as the most common question I get from other people in my life is "You still play that game? Why." I do play locally or like using it when I'm out of my normal area and can tell if an area is super popular depending on the number of poke stops. Local raiding is hard, not enough people and now it's impossible to get my online friends to get remote passes to help me out.

Since the new updates, I can't get in to play. Every time the game loads, it'll stop halfway with loading or it'll load and then immediately crash. I played it when it came out and then got back into it in 2018 and I never had a problem quite like this. I also feel that the update with the Avatar changes make it especially hard to control because of all the enhanced stuff. Really want to keep playing but I can't keep playing if I keep experiencing this; please fix it.

I'm switching to 1*... it's been crashing for me lately. It's super frustrating and I've tried so many things to fix it on my end. app is constantly crashing as soon as I get in. I've cleared cache, force stopped, uninstalled and reinstalled, I've restarted my phone, I've emptied my storage, I've deleted my other apps and nothing helps. this really ruined my experience at Pokemon go fest Seattle. please help.

Team Rocket are still not balanced for gameplay with the recommended party group. First part still stands. Next is that Routes are pretty much non-existent, OG players should have immediate access to new features the moment they are released. Can't use any routes if none exist, especially when players who have been around from the beginning can't make use of new features. 2/5 still stands.

Really disappointing that they changed the PokeStop range back. There used to be 2 within range of my work, but now I can't reach them, and I'm not about to start running in and out every 5 minutes. I may play during events, but unless they fix it back that's gonna be it. It's a good thing Pokemon Unite just came out.

Just noticed that I'd given GO a 5-Star -- well, not any longer. Niantic is so unreasonably obsessed with the way THEY want the game to be played, the result is they mostly ignore their player base and sometimes willfully flip them off. It's sad, really. At 6 years, if they don't find new ways to play the game, ways their players WANT to play the game, they're gonna eventually lose it all, and it will be no fault but their own. 😒💙

Over the years the game has gone in and out. I never had so many issues trying just to log in to my account! And now today having the same issues and when the game does load and a pokemon is touched it disappears. Perhaps all my hard work can just go right down the drain and I'll stop spending the money and playing. It's disheartening because this connected me and my family over the years.

I used to play this game every so often, nothing serious. When covid hit I had even less opportunity to play. Thankfully Niantic made some very useful changes to make the game safer and easier to play. And I began to play a lot and actually spend money on the game. Well, today in the middle of the worst spike of cases in over a year, they reversed those changes. A total "Screw you and your safety" to all it's players. Well, screw them and their game instead. I'm done unless they reinstate them.

Fun game, but there are a few issues. they really need to work on variety with 1,2 and 3 star raids. It's supposed to be one of maybe three or four pokemon in each tier, yet I always see the same one every time. Same with research reward encounters, there are 8 possibilities with what can appear but I only ever get Suicune or Entei. it's frustrating because it's SUPPOSED to be random

The developers have ruined this game. Been playing this game since launch since 2016 and have absolutely loved this game when it actually works. Consistent bugs, crashes, and errors in the game make it unplayable at times. Developers have made increasingly worse decisions with the game making it nearly impossible to play unless you have 4-5 phones, tons of free time and money, and live in a place with a lot of stuff nearby. If you have not started this game, don't try it.

I love the game, but there is an annoying glitch that I guess hasn't been addressed yet, unless it's just my phone. On my Galaxy S4, every time I play the game with full phone sounds and notifications active and another app sends me an audio notification, like an email alert, causes all sounds in the game to fail. It is only remedied when I completely close the game and reopen. Any one else have this problem?

Changing my rating. I understand the goal is to get out and explore. But it's at a point where Niantic is PENALIZING players who don't have that opportunity. Must be nice to be wealthy & healthy, and have unlimited resources for getting out there. Btwn increasing remote raid pass cost and "fixing" a "bug" that allowed players to see more spawns, I'm just angry. Wouldn't it be more player-friendly to incentivize "going places" rather than penalizing those who can't? Do you even listen to people?

I love the game. I've been playing since 2016. But, Niantic has issues. If you're casual, it's fun and addictive. If you're at all hardcore, it's irritating. The game crashes. Items dissappear. Pokémon you spend hours finding never show up. If you spend money and have an issue, you get little compensation. My main issues are with how the game is run, and if you only play minimally, you may be fine. But for me, the rating can't be higher until all the glitches are solved/compensated.

The game is still very fun if you enjoy catching pokemon on walks or cratching that pokè itch. Yet limitations can be annoying some examples, long distance raid passes instead of any raid pass, you can't trade with people unless if you're close, even though you can battle and send gifts long distance, and a lot of special events are pay to play. if they fixed these so that it wasn't based off of the very best being those who pay the most I would rate it higher.

While I find myself in here off and on they really missed an opportunity to make a game with some depth like the Gameboy version that came out years back. I think this can be seen in the huge interest initially and subsequent drop off as fans realized it wasn't gaining much of the features they had hoped it would gain. I really don't know why fighting hasn't been revamped and not to mention a PvP system hasn't been added.

This is a terrible "game". It gives you just enough stuff to do to pass itself off as interactive but the actual gameplay is one of the worst things I've ever seen. Like a certain Pokemon? Too bad, theres a good chance its useless for battles. Dislike the ones that are great for battles? Too bad, if you're not using them you cant compete. The raids arent frequent enough and now that the hype died down theres a chance you'll never beat some. Horrible design.

After a VERY rough starting year that got me so frustrated I quit playing for 2 years.... The game a seriously improved! I'd give it a 3/5, mostly because rural gameplay is TERRIBLE. The devs really need to base spawns on how many people are active in an area at any given moment. My husband, friend, and I have ALL logged in at our rural house and left the game on for HOURS, and never improved the spawn rates. I can't afford to drive 1.5 hrs into the nearest city anytime I want to play.

This app sucks!! It probably would be a great app to get people out side to do some walking... IF YOU COULD GET IT TO LOAD! UPDATE... Since I wrote this review, the game has definitely improved for me. I cant walk so much anymore but I still play as much as I can. It has become a permanent game on my devices. I think they didn't have the compasity on their servers in the beginning to handle the multitude of people that was downloading and playing non-stop.I definitely would recommend this game

I have really enjoyed playing for over two years. However, the game has many glitches which Niantic falls short on fixing. These actually cost the player money. Ninantic will throw a few free passes at everyone to passify the grumbling. But they make money regardless and have little incentive to fix. After the reduced distance between stops, I play maybe 25% of what I used to play. I'm upset to learn from data miners that they intend to bring the distance back but charge for it. Time to quit.

This game still has some of the same bugs since launch. Bots run the game. Constant problems with the raid system can leave you out of the raid but take your pass. Niantic support can't read English and responds only in boilerplate, often for the wrong issue, and mark cases complete despite no resolution. As far as gameplay, it's the most inconvenient contradictive game you could ever play. While moving in real life, you need to stop to play but you need to move to get incentives.

Loved the game since 2016. Recent updates doubling the cost of remote raid passes has completely taken away any desire ive had to play this game. I live in an area with not many pokestops much less gyms. Remote raids where how I got certain pokemon. Now I feel its pointless to play. Thanks for introducing something awesome Niantic...just to take it away. Disappointed is an understatement.

I love this game! It helps give me incentives to go outside and exercise and be active. It doesn't even feel like a lot once I'm playing. We've walked over 7 miles one day just playing the ggame!! I stand by my original review but would love to see the ability to sort my pokemon by category i.e-ice, water, fire etc. Would make finding that perfect pokemon for battles so much easier!

As a kid, I loved playing Pokémon with my friends and pretended we were trainers. This app takes that to a whole new level. I absolutely love it! Just curious though, will Niantic add more Pokémon such as the rest of the originals and the black and white series? Also, will we be able to individually battle other trainers anytime without having to always go to a gym? Hope to find out soon. Overall, amazing game. I love it.

Niantic has made substantial changes and fixes. Many good, others are simply different. My main frustrations with the game remain: The battle system is a shallow imitation of the gameplay Pokemon fans have come to expect from the series. Money sinks are everywhere, which is standard fare for a f2p game, but the core gameplay is so devoid of substance that the only sense of progress comes from building your inventory, which is exactly where Niantic builds their paywalls.

Recently, even though I have ALL the notifications turned off, I keep getting this "finding nearby Pokemon" notification. I don't have Po-Go+ and I really only open the app occasionally at this point (poke stops and gems on PRIVATE PROPERTY with nothing that can be done is broken/unfair and should be considered malicious manipulation of the game, like changing locations, but it isn't). Attempting to close the notification does nothing, muting the notification does nothing.

The walking part of the game is fine, but the Go Battle League is terribly made and maintained. It's based on 'gaming the system' and manipulating the lag with cryptic unseen variables like "move lag, CMP ties, real attack stats" etc that are not visible in the game, but must be looked up on external websites. Also, the top-rated battlers are frequently 'pay to win' very limited-time or legendary Pokemon and are structured in a way to make you spend ($) resources to compete. Truly awful. Scam.

With the most recent few updates the game has been buggy and crashes frequently. My phone isn't powerful but it used to work fine. Most recent update causes game to immediately crash upon opening. Can't do anything, even after troubleshooting. Very disappointed. Considering uninstalling it for a few to let these bugs be worked out. If they aren't then this may be the last time I play... Ever.

I have been playing on and off since 2016 and playing daily for two years now. 1. Pretty boring. You walk around and collect Pokémon. They tend to escape and flee randomly though making the process very frustrating. I walked for a mile and did not see a single Pokémon, but when you start the game it spawns 3-5, making it questionable why you would go out. Eventually I ran out of Pokéballs - I guess the game doesn't want me to play.

It's fun for a little while but it suffers from a lack of depth, and it is a grind. Most Pokémon games have three major components: - Finding and catching Pokémon. - Battling and training Pokémon. - Direct peer-to-peer multiplayer. It would be okay if one of these components were weak or overly simple, but all three of these components are weak and incredibly simple. It would be much better if Pokémon Go shared more characteristics with the Gameboy games.

A great game for a Pokemon fan, has a lot of social potential and works as a great booster to get you moving. The app itself does crash often, almost to a point that its considered normal to have a few crashes per day. When it works its great, but its a shame it doesnt run as a smoothly as it could. PoGo is a deeply flawed as a game for many reasons that most people have covered here, but(!) It's perhaps the only game to recapture the sense of adventure and wonder we had as children. Playing this game has frustrated me no end with all the bugs and problems, but through it all it has also made me extremely happy and I've met many great people along the way. I thoroughly recommend it.

The game have greatly improved, but the PvP is poorly executed. If it was more traditional combat (as additional option) there would be even more people playing it. (real place near you) find (some pokemon/team rocket/item) and a chance for the quest to escalate. Overall it is a good game, with room for improvement. Also where is the team battle system?

Since the last update it has gotten even worse to a point where I have to restart the game every few minutes because it suddenly stops being able to find my location.

As a big Pokémon fan, I played this game since the day it came out. The biggest problem is how much the game forces you to play in certain ways to complete certain tasks. I'm not a fan of the forced multiplayer for raids and forced walking for tasks which is not always convenient or safe in my area. Other similar games have more to do while you are not moving and this game sorely lacks that. Finally, the pricing and lack of opportunity to get in-game currency is disappointing.

Game feels like a Beta best case scenario. It now has fewer features than it was released with. I've been plagued by glitches and server issues since the day of release. With many added features I would say it feels like a fully fledged idea with lots of new content/ events that manage to keep the game engaging.

Amazing concept, learning new places and monuments I've never noticed before! Pokemon are also mainly in the city, which isn't very logic. No point in traveling around, just head to a big city. One of my favourite games, even all these years after it came out. Harder to free-play these days. I'm forced to sign in again, but it can never authenticate my information. It never says I entered anything incorrectly, just that it can't authenticate. I'm forced to reset my password every time. Niantic, get yourself together.

I've played this game for years off and on. Each time it's been better than before, but for some reason as of the last few updates, the game has become unbearably laggy. It has reached a point where it is borderline unplayable. I have adjusted all the in game settings and my phone settings, but it's still extremely slow. I've burned so many pokeballs and resources just trying to throw them or attack, but because of the lag you completely miss, or your pokemon faints because it didn't register.

Having an absolutely awful experience. On top of the 10+ minute wait times, it white-screens whenever I go to catch a pokémon. I went to change my username (as I had an old account) and I had to reload 5+ times. The keyboard would not open as I went to change my username and when it did, it would close the keyboard after typing one letter. Not worth it on android - I've tried to download it on an alternate device so we'll see how that goes.

Ahead of the release of this game there were alot of different features that were promised to be delivered only a short amount of time (some months) after the release of the game. Features such as Trainer vs Trainer, Common Loot System for every Trainer no matter the Trainer's current cordinates, a gamestyle where you can team up and make friends with your Pokémon and a great story you can relate to. None of these things have come out yet, and that's why the game is loosing interest.

To be honest, I waited for three years after release and tested the app on four different devices before I could eventually play and it was definitely worth the wait 😁 really enjoying, I was just hoping maybe for an update where Pokemon that have enough candies to evolve are highlighted when you view all your Pokemon, it would make it so much easier than having to sit, sort and go through each and every one (btw, I have about 200 so far), please please consider it, I think it would help a ton.

It's an amazing game that encourage you to explore places you haven't thought of visiting and make new friends. But it's also about pure luck. You could be spending time, money, energy, & battery life grinding, battling and other stuff yet still left frustrated with the results. While other players just take less effort and get way better pokemons. That is so not fair!

I downloaded GO a while ago and I absolutely loved it. However, I reached a stage of the game where it was impossible for me to progress; I had no Poké Ball left in stock and due to living in a rural area, I could not access gyms and PokéStops, which are an important part of the game. It would be quite nice if more Poké Stop and Gyms could be created. Even then, I rate it five stars because it is a great game overall!

The game is more fun now when they made more Pokémon spawn in suburban areas. The thing I don't like is the combat. Very tedious, boring and repetitive with just tapping and dodging. If they made it so that you could collect TMs and learn your Pokémon moves when reaching a certain CP, it'd make the game so much more worth to be fighting gyms as well as adding more stuff to collect and show off to your friends.

The game has a huge focus on micro transactions, the more you pay the better you play. As a result the game suffers unnecessarily from it. I don't mind paying for a game, but the current model is terrible. A subscription would be a much better payment model. The recent decision to revert some of the more than year long covid related changes in the name of profit at the cost of, not only enjoyment of the game, but also the safety of the game, has prompted me to make this 2 star review.

Good game if you're a pokemon fan, otherwise I'd be less confident recommending it. The game is somewhat past it's prime, both in terms of popularity (summer 2016) and ideal player experience (the company is actively rolling back improvements made during 2020 which aid rural and remote play because they can't sell as much data if you have to walk around less). It's still enjoyable if you did enjoy it in it's prime, but I don't know a lot of people who have stuck with it.

Horrible! This has happened so much that I decided to write this review. I always have an issue with the app hanging and freezing at the loading page. This has been like this at least 2 years now! And I've given up on this game. If Niantic wants people to give this a good rating, better get your issues together. Oh and it's super laggy too. I'm using OPPO F1s. There are only a few good days where they app runs really smooth. This is not worth my time anymore.

The game currently is truly bad. I used to like this game a lot for more than 3 or 4 years. But with the new update it's horrendous. While the addition of customisation feature is not a bad addition. There is no longer the male and female option. Also my character looks ugly compared to before. Unless theses mistakes are fixed I am not playing this game any more. Just give me the old art back.

The concept is great, it was a massive hit and even gained news coverage. And yeah, going out to capture pokemon can actually be fun. But the problems? You can't fight with friends at your own leisure. You cant , say visit a friend's house and have just a short, friendly match. The only way you can fight are through gyms which is tedious. Plus you need data to play the game, if you don't have data then you can't progress whatsoever, which is off-putting for many, including me

I love this game, been playing since it came to the UK. However certain things are really starting to annoy me, for example, pokemon with incredibly low CP are somehow able to break out of ultra balls many times! Also, when battling, there should be an option to decline the mystery pokemon that you win. I've just used 60 pokeballs trying to catch one, all of my berries, multiple ultra balls and all of my great balls and STILL I haven't caught it! And I cant battle again till I've got it!

Enjoyable if you're out and about a lot. Game sometimes hangs when you click on a wild pokemon- requiring you to restart the game and lose the pokemon you were just trying to catch. The AR scan task is quite irritating, particularly if you don't have access to get exactly where the marker is. Even when you can- I've stood on an AR gym many times and it still tells me to get closer to scan it, though there was physically no way for me to get on top of it more than I already was.

I enjoy playing. I am disappointed that our pokemon cannot get better by fighting in the gyms, I want more varied options for my character, I want pokemon battles to look more like the game (or a strategy type game would be awesome) and my phone keeps freezing up while I walk or when I'm catching pokemon, requiring endless restarts. Hopefully, this new update will take care of some of those issues.

It's actually a good game, but there are some things that need to be fixed. If you attack a gym and clear two rounds alone, and in the last round, there is another player fighting with you from another team, then you may have to wait for them to place their Pokémon first, even though you started the gym fight first. It's quite frustrating because then you have to clear the gym again. And if you have no luck, other players come and place their Pokémon, so you have to battle more Pokémon.

I really love this game. But because I live in a town/not a city, there are so few gyms and pokestops in the area. Specifically where I live you cannot even see a gym on the screen, and there are 3 pokestops on the edges. I have to travel quite a few kilometers to find one. Been playing incredibly hard though and finally on level 35. But I'm growing tired of the limited experience from home since I can't do remote raids like other people can from their homes.

Game is good and so is the graphics. But the game keeps on freezing. I had to reinstall but it's the same issue. either scrolling through my inventory, pokemons or even doing raid battle and capturing, the game freezes for no reason. Cache is too many from this game i have to delete it everytime. Next time make the app 1gb plus so that all game resources are already in and no need to load. Please niantic read my review. I'm not the only one experiencing this problem.

I played this game from launch until about two years ago, when I took a hiatus from it. After redownloading the game, I am appalled and horrified by the changes forced on players by Niantic. Adventure sync on Android used to be integrated in a way where it would only gather info on how far you walked. Now it needs to read your location all the time. That's way too much info. Need I even mention the remote raid changes? Pure corporate greed and sad to see a game I enjoyed so much fall so far.

Fun game that encourages me to go out and walk! There are a lot of folks talking about bugs here, but I haven't been having problems. My main gripe is spoofers ruining the fun for people who want to play the game as intended. Some moderation so far as this is concerned would be really great. I know spoofers converge online to cooperate. There has to be a way to crack down on that. It really does make it frustrating sometimes. I'll be playing for as long as it's available!

At this stage, the game has no storyline. Its only objective is to collect as many pokemon as possible. Controlling gyms offers the opportunity to collect a tiny number of in-game currency, but that's it. There's quite a few game features related to walking distance, but the game still can't track walked distance properly.

pokemon go is essentially unplayable now. all vehicle (high speed) play is entirely eliminated which is where the game was most playable originally. On top of that, ever since the beginning, the game was useless if you didn't live in a major city because you would never see any pokemon around where you lived. I'm not sure how the issues it originally had were never fixed but its actually gotten worse over time. This game needs a major overhaul and a re tooling if it's ever going to be any good.

It's fun, but the pricing is interesting. Most games on the market will give you discount when you buy in game currency which means the more you buy the cheaper it cost per unit. To pretend they care for your wallet. For example, if you pay $1 for 100 coins and for 1200 coins, instead of paying $12 usually you pay less let's say $11. But in Pokemon GO, you pay $1 for 100 coins, and for 1200 coins, you pay $15, which is more expensive. They don't even pretend! They want it bad!

Game is awesome, it let's me live my childhood dream of finding Pokémon in "real life" and I thank you for that 👍. Everything is great except that there is one thing that is bugging me and that is that the roads do not show up on my map. The Pokémon, gyms, and Pokestops do but the roads in my area don't. So it basically looks like I'm playing in a big field of grass haha. Please fix, just a small issue but it's bugging me. Thanks!!! EDIT: Thanks for the fix, game and updates are awesome.

So much potential wasted. Niantic was responsible for the first thing humanity came to world peace, yet they failed. I've played the game since it's launch and even though it was always littered with bugs, but it was okay because it was fun. They managed to improve the game even more during the pandemic, making the game more accessible to the less able. After that it all went downhill. They slowly removed or limited every good new feature. Last straw was doubling the prices in the in game shop.

I played for a few days here (after 2 year hiatus) and I will be putting it down forever. The pay-to-win portion of this game is out of control. This game has diversified in so many things to keep things competitive and incentivise buying stuff in the shop to keep your edge. All we wanted was a real world pokemon where you walk, catch, train, & fight Pokemons. Shame on you Niantic.

It was enjoyable enough when I first started playing with my wife, but just like the pokemon company itself, the game has become stale, and I see very little interest in jumping back into it. The avatar changes were bad, but that's only one of many other problems with the game now. From the overpriced shop to the constant lag issues.

I played this game for years now and im starting to enjoy it less ans less, simply because, with the recent update, Niantic are refusing to take into consideration players that either cant attend in person rais due to personal difficulties, or simply not having a large enough local community to deal with harder content, such as legendary and mega raids. However if this huge part of the game is to be overlooked, its still a pretty good game, but still, not as inclusive as it was and should be.

No help or tutorial at the start was dumb. And finding Pokémon takes forever, Thanks to the fact I don't live in a city. Great idea on straight up abandoning the countryside. Plus getting pokeballs is dumb, I get one or two from a stop. Should be given way more than that to be considered long term playable without paying which is clearly its main focus... I jump in and out but it's mostly just garbage and something to do for no real reason.

The game itself is great fun. Very well thought and gets more and more features. Regular events and a very nice community around it. The implementation on the other hand is poor at best. The game is full of bugs, kicking you out of raid battles for no good reason, errors out in the middle of anything. They obviously make a lot of money on the in-game purchases, I don't really get how they can low-ball their infrastructure.

If you're playing this game ensure you have phone data to spare! Big data and battery hog. My only real complaint in regards to gameplay is the amount of time it takes to collect in-game currency. Of course the app needs to make money somehow, but only 50 coins can be gathered a day from gyms, making the process of collecting coins to expand the inventory (VERY necessary) quite tedious. Otherwise lots of fun, and a great motivator for getting some exercise in your day-to-day!

This is BS. I really want to like this game. I like Pokemon, the art style is appealing, there are some cool concepts in here plus lots of potential. But more than 2 years after release this is still a technical abomination. Poor performance on new phones, battery killer & constant freezes & errors: "Network Error", the infamous "Unknown Error" or, my favorite, lo and behold, "Error (0)"! Might as well tell me "F... YOU!" With all the $$$ they couldn't do a better job? REALLY? ERROR (0), I say!

Updated from my previous review (from 2016: 4 -> 3 stars). The gameplay has got more fun, and the previous issues are resolved. However the game is becoming more pay-to-play than it used to be. You now have to buy some special researches (not using the in game currency), and it is harder than ever to earn in game currency. It takes 3 days of acquiring the maximum daily coins in order to afford a single incubator, which is virtually impossible as it requires other people to beat your gyms daily.

Came back to the game after almost 6 years. Lots of new features. Game feels rewarding. Gym system is much better and you can easily get your 50 coins everyday. Only reason not 5* is that its pretty pay to win. I would give it 5 if you could get 150 coins a day. Would balance out the prices of things a bit and allow you to keep up with the people who spend a lot of money on the game.

Firstly, the game wanted to update while I was casually taking over a gym. It's the closest gym to my house. The game wouldn't let me play until I updated, which took about twenty minutes. From then on I can't even open the app, it just stays on the loading screen. I've tried uninstalling and reinstalling the app, and I've also restarted my phone, but nothings working. The game was actually good before this. I genuinely love the game, but now I can't play, which is lowkey depressing.

If they go through with their latest round of planned price increases, it will be cost prohibitive to play. I am planning on using up whatever I have left for coins, and won't be buying any more. Will absolutely not spend over $1 each for a remote raid pass, let alone the $1.75 they are planning. They're crazy to implement these changes during a recession. Their egg hatch game is also still a weak point. Was a fun distraction for 7 years but I suppose all good things must come to and end.

I spend far too much time on this game. Following the most recent update, however, this is likely to change. The buddy section no longer loads, meaning that it will take longer to upgrade and will also deny "gifts" that it brings. It was bad enough that you decided that we couldn't play long distance raids, but this is ridiculous. Kinda defeats the object when you can't play the whole game. Thumbs down, Niantic.

Good game. Very fun and it does an awsome job of getting you out and about going on adventures. Even if your just stuck inside on a booring day, you can do remote raids or trainer battles. I've been playing this for years now. Every now and then I get GPS signal glitches but they fix in a few days. I think it would be cool to see a 2v2 mode come to the game some time soon though. Pokemon fashion shows would be pretty cool to see in the game too. Overall I rate it 4/5

2016 Very addictive. I can't log in half the time but when I can I can't fault the game. My dogs never been walked so much. New review. 2022 still playing on and off. My son is into it now. Sadly though I can't seem to upload pokestop scans, it just crashes and the adventure sync doesn't work for either of us. Other then that. Brilliant game. X

Please create a rule so that players cannot take over a gym they have just been kicked out of within a certain amount of time. We have one local player who will appear (driving) within minutes of being kicked out of a gym, no matter the time of day, or location in our town, and take the gym back. It is making the game boring for other players, who are no longer getting any joy out of taking over gyms, and I will stop playing soon if this continues.

Can't even play the game anymore, every time it loads up, it freezes, no matter what. Like this game has been out for 2 years, how can you not fix these issues by now. Honestly the bugs have gotten worse over the years. First it was just a server problem, but now it's the actual game itself with all its glitches and bugs. Plz fix this game so everyone can enjoy it.

Have been playing since the game came out and never experienced any issues - until now. The latest update has screwed the game for me. I can no longer catch pokemon. If I have AR turned on I can't catch anything no matter how hard I try, and when I turn it off the game freezes and I have to force stop on the app. I have a OnePlus phone with Android. Please please fix this!!

Fun enough to play for a grind-based game, but there are plenty of bugs and support are notoriously unhelpful so beware. I had free items simply disappear over time which I let slide, but when a paid-for rare item failed to be added to one I'd keeping for months, Niantic refused to acknowledge that 1+1=2 and kept me at 1, despite agreeing I hadn't used one in recent history and claiming the new one had been added. So enjoy it, have fun, but don't expect to be respected by the developer.

Playing was fun at the start because of the steps-tracker. But not being able to TRACK a mon is beyond frustrating!! EDIT: New tracking system is worse! Showing ONLY Pokestops encourages driving if they are too far away, instead of walking to NEARBY pokemon. Can only track if near a Pokestop. Been playing since the beginning and am a dedicated player. If I didn't have a spawn spot in my house or work, I wouldn't play at all now. Please, BRING BACK TRACKING!!!

Niantic had implemented fantastic changes that made the game interesting and fun for players in rural areas or in situations that make travel/walking difficult. They have decided to turn their backs on all those players by prioritizing in-person raids and geolocation data. I am disappointed by these changes that make the wonderful Pokemon universe less accessible for a wide range of players (non-city folks). I will reinstall the game if Niantic shows consideration for its player base.

Pokemon Go has come along way since its beginning. It runs smoother, has more to do and the events are great. There is still alot of activity even in the smaller suburbs or towns and the seasonal roster and event roster pokemon are a great edition. My only complaint is that the character is the same for everyone. There are so many types of characters in the game from pokefans, scientists, bug catchers and fisherman. They should be entered as an avatar for players.

Tracker update, lack of communication, shut down of 3rd party apps, curve ball bonus removal. A lot of the things that made this game good have been thrown out of the window. EDITED IN 2019: The game has eventually gotten so much better and I have amended my review to reflect that. Its infinitely more stable than it was at release, trading, friends, raids and more pokemon than ever, while fixing pokemon tracking and the many bugs that were plaguing it in the beginning.

Like many others, I started this game in 2016 and dropped out of it just as the bugs continued to happen around that time. I came back to pogo in 2018 and had a blast till 2022. The game became stale. Remote raid passes because more expensive and limited and some players just don't use money for the game. Grinding in gyms was already hard enough. Disappointed that I will miss the friends I've made around the world. You know when was the best time for pogo? During covid. Use those updates.

Greedy slimballs. Uninstalling game right now, I play the game mostly in the summer, as a way to get active. But the changes to the remote raids basically makes it unsustainable to play in the winter. If they wanted more activity in person, they could have left it at the 5 limit. But the fact that they raised the price, shows their intentions is greed. No consideration for players and different communities and region or safety. It's a global game, excludes major chunks of the population.

This is one of the best mobile games ever made. However it is not perfect, one problem I, and many others I know has is the types of pokemon in our area. I RARELY get anything other than pidgeys, ratattas and spearows and nothing else. Please could you increase the chance of getting better and rarer Pokemon as I get nothing but the same boring things. Also could you also add something that shows you the pokemon in that area rather than the sightings thing? Its kinda annoying.

Good game. I like the feeling of being able to catch Pokémon in real life, but there are a few things which mess it up for me. Pokémon don't spawn randomly anymore, only in specific locations. This makes it harder if you live nowhere near any pokéstops. Also, only higher leveled players can catch higher cp Pokémon, which annoys me because my friend is lv 26 and I'm only level 12. Overall the game is good, but a few changes should be made.(:

Awesome game IF YOU HAVE DATA AND FRIENDS TO ADD MIND YOU. you basically need friends so that you can send gifts and receive them. That's how you end up with a lot of stuff if your bag. Also, the game ends up making you spend money to upgrade your bag, I haven't gone further than level 27 yet so I'm not sure whether I'll need to spend more or not. If so than I can't see myself playing this game a whole lot longer. I like how you have to get out to actually play the game.

Pretty fun game. However, you need to live in the center of big cities to get the most out of it. I can understand pokéstops being as they are now, but the logical thing would be having pokemon outside, in the actual wilderness... Can't play solo anymore, Gyms and raids require you team up with others, but when there is no one on your level around (everyone is at high levels nowadays it seems)...

I have been a dedicated player for many years, even though not everything has been as fun, like the first few years, I have continued to play daily! I have spent money and time all to have my Account hacked, and because I got 1 or 2 questions (questions that many can get incorrect!) I am no longer valid to confirm I am the owner of my own account, even if I present payment informations, pokemon and more. tried customer support, several times, all get told to make a new account... Just horrible

I am really enjoying the game and would love to give it a good rating, but I am constantly getting issues, crashing, freezing up and graphical issues too. These are all things that I can work around as they don't stop my progress. But the main issue I have, is Pokémon in gyms, they will be in there for 12 or more hours, get knocked then get knocked out. I'll get the notification to get pokecoins, but when I look, I haven't received any, this has happened a lot of times it's stopping me raiding.

I've been playing this game since day 1 and I have never before seen a game company so fit to be dunked on as this. Niantic have shown time and time again that they simply only care about getting money and gathering your data. Recent changes to their raid system and shop have made it impossible for many of the long term players to actively enjoy the game without spending ludicrous amounts of money. Do not download the game until these issues are addressed by Niantic (which they never will be)

There are many issues that compromise the fundamental enjoyment of the game. There needs to be some sort of tracking. It doesn't have to be a specific location but at least bring something in that allows you to know if you're getting close or too far away. Lack of variety of pokemon spawning in rural areas is an issue. The gym update means anyone can take a gym. The new buddy system is an attempt to stop you hoarding useful berries and getting rare candies more easily.

It has been 4 years since the game released and numerous features have been added such as raiding, trading and PvP. On the downside, Niantic has proven to be an incompetent and greedy company, introducing new bugs every update and not resolving bugs that have been around for ages, while also delaying or even blocking player progress behind a paywall. The game is great if you're a fan of Pokémon or have a group of friends/good community to play with. Otherwise, steer clear from this cash grab.

My old review was a little bitter and is now out of date, so here's a new one. I love the game and log in many times daily. Mostly due to my love of pokemon. The game has made me get more exercise, visit new places and make new friends, so it's achieved what the developers want. However, there are too many little issues that stop it getting 5* Mostly its trivial stuff, but there's enough of it to make it add up.

There are still some frustrating stuff , that seem easy to fix and provide a better experience. Pokemon in gyms that are not challenged can stay there for months. There should be a way to claim them back. Less trade challenges please. Some of us don't have a lot of friends, who play the game, around. Also, pvp is pretty boring. Other than that, fun game.
screen goes black for first Pokemon catch and requires me to restart the app.

Great game but there is a problem within it that's kind of laughable. If you were to buy PokeCoins with real money, its gets more expensive the more you buy, rather than cheaper for more as most games do. For example, 100 PokeCoins in .99c, yet 550 PokeCoins is roughly $7. The trend continues with higher values as well. As you can see, you get more value if you were to buy multiple at .99c. Really weird mechanic and so surprised it has not been changed yet.

Was a 5* game but Niantic have run the game into the ground. The game has been profusely limited in what you can do daily, or weekly. It has turned into a complete and utter pay to win game except the prices have skyrocket as well, and even then they have put a cap on how many raids you can do. With these new changes they have basically cut rural players, disabled players and players who have busy lives from the game point blank. I have uninstalled, and I certainly wouldn't recommend.

malfunctioning GPS is one thing, and not letting us log in is another, but to not even load the game and just stuck at the Niantic screen? This is a new low for an update error. I thought I've seen the worst this game has to offer, but turns out I'm wrong. I guess I won't be playing and discovering the new Sinnoh Pokémon and evolutions for a while.

Well, this is a great idea for a Pokemon game to have people going outside! But, the problem is that, in the new trading system, it costs way too much stardust, even as you level up friendship level, especially shinies, legendaries and new Pokemon. I would understand if it were around 50000-75000 stardust for good friends, but it is so much more! Also we need to implement trading items, please.

To be honest i didnt expect this. They added gyms and pokestops making it possible to have tons of pokeballs. When i quit the only thing you could do was to catch and to battle (in gyms) now you can trade, battle each other, send gifts to friends and more. An lastly but the most important change is that they added a variety of pokemon to my area making the game enjoyable. Overall the game became great for my area and i want to believe for other areas like mine.

It's a lot of fun game. I enjoy that I 've get out my room and search for new pokemons. The new feature, trainer battle is owesome. But, I've found its difficult to find other trainers nearby. It will be so much easier and helpfull if you add some feature like a radar to detect where is the other trainer around and also we (players) can challenge them without say hello to them (in real). It is weird sometimes that you have to make contact with strangers only to playing a game. Thank you.

I couldn't even get onto the app. It would load, and then I'd try to make an account and it would take to long to load. I would leave my phone on for hours, and the app wouldn't load the screen where I could make an account with Google. I don't like the apps overall experience either. Groudons are extremely hard to catch, and you can't find any starter pokemon. The only other time I found so thing else was the eevees. This app is a waste of time, and a waste of space.

The playing mechanics are great for a mobile game and the concept finally got me to excersise willingly. However like for most other players, the servers are down half the time (or more). Knowing the amount of hype this game had before release, the servers should've been prepared for something like this. Please fix this issue as I personally find it the only thing from seeing Pokemon GO as a 5-star app.

The game itself is very good, but when you want to log back in or create another account, it keeps asking you for an "adult" email address for a child account, but as soon as you want to create your adult account, they still show you have to enter a parent's email address. It's illogical and totally annoying. I wanted to play again for the nostalgia, but the desire quickly disappeared as soon as I struggled for more than 15 minutes. So good luck.

Its the same game for so many years. Nothing good ever happens n. Progress is so slow, It's feels like monotonous work on a monday and its all for the sake of a cash grab for niantic. From being a hardcore player now i've just limited the game to community day's, get a shiny and done till the next one. Keep an alarm on the phone, keep a lure for 1/2 or 1 hour and get like 1-3 shines and done. If it wasnt for this i wouldnt even open the game anymore. The focus to reward ratio is too less.

I used to love playing pokemon go and I still play it now, but more and more features exclude players in remote areas. Thinking about raiding (at least we have remote Raids now) and now the next one the routes. I am living on an island with a couple of gyms and about 20 pokestops, we finally were able to create routes ourselves but it's taking forever to get them approved, I feel like the game has turned into an app where the money making has priority over the actual enjoyment of the players.

The thing is, this game would be great if there was any form of consistency to the catch rates. A rare/strong/legendary pokemon i get will be difficult to catch, it's part of the fun. But when it's taking 5+ berries and balls to catch a freakin' Caterpie -well, you see where I'm going with this. Also, i live in a big city and the calabre of the pokemon available to catch is garbage 99% of the time, so i dread to think how awful it is out in the sticks.

It used to be good but Niantic went full predatory mode. Their prices keeps coming up (from 100 to 195 tokens for remote raids. That's stupidly huge). They offer special loot boxes with better rewards but only if you don't have enough token so you're forced to buy if you want the deal. If you have a lot of tokens tho, you can't have that deal... They don't care about their player base. I don't recommend playing this game.

Love the game for someone like myself but upon thinking about it the mechanics of it make it incredibly uninclusive , I know that's cryptic but unfortunately the character limit means I can't go into full detail about the issue, I even had helpful suggestions on how you could fix the issue and still have the game be entirely fair for all players. As its not really fair to point out something such as that without thinking it through yourself. Anyways. That's my review. Probably no one cares lol.

I've been four years without playing it and because the game seems more attractive now, I'm back. But Niantic isn't really trying to adapt it in regards to Covid-19 quarentine. It seems a fun game, it brings me back to my childhood but it has a big flaw. The only game I like to play. Lots to do and fun But there are to many glitches and errors and lately the game has become automated, makes the experience feel less real. Which ultimately makes it just another game. A month ago it wasn't like that. Catching Pokémon in Raids are also a no go. You will get 1 out of every 5 battles. Gets expensive.

So far so good. The graphics and gameplay, though simple, is surely addicting and enjoyable. It lags some of the time maybe because of my mobile connection. Im waiting for the new tacking system and the IV calculator. I am also looking forward for the 2nd generation pokemon to come out. Keep it up Niantic! 1/8/2021 I am trying to get back to the game when I heard you can now level up to 50. Its still fun, more tasks and things to do. But why do I feel like this has been a pay to win game?

The game is great in general but I've found a few fundamental issues with trading that could be improved. There is no warning in game that you cannot trade back your Pokémon, therefore causing me to lose one of my best ones when attempting to get a lucky Pokémon. This is poor game design and user experience. This could be solved by allowing trade backs, with possibly a cool down of 30 days so as to not take advantage. Also needs a popup warning before confirming trade.

Niantic actively makes it harder for people to play the game by pushing in person play features and making it harder to play remotely (less incense spawns when stationary, remote raid pass prices going up). If you live in a rural environment, are disabled, or even if there's really bad/dangerous weather outside, you can't play at all. This does not make for an inclusive game and overall the changes push people away rather than bring them together.

I've played this since it was released officially in the UK. Since then, it's gained so many features that are fundamental to Pokemon, that it is essentially a fully fledged Pokemon game in its own right, rather than a quick money grabber. It occasionally suffers reliability issues but those tend to get resolved soon after, and it's adapted well to lockdown measures from COVID. Overall, if you like Pokémon, there's no reason to miss out on playing this.

I've been a dedicated Pokémon Go player for years, but the recent price increase of Remote Raid Passes is really disappointing. These passes were a great way to stay connected with friends and participate in raids from anywhere, especially during the pandemic. Now, with the higher prices, it feels like the game is becoming less accessible for many players. I hope Niantic reconsiders this decision and makes the game more affordable again!

I've been playing this a lot, while partaking in my daily walks out and about the neighborhood. I've not been a Pokefan much in the past but really feel like this game rewards you for getting out and doing some exercise. Like the Ingress game it's based on, there's strategic locations around your neighborhood you can visit to find resources, that you can use to capture Pokémon and to improve the ones you have. You don't have to fight other people if you don't want to either, which is nice.

It's a fun, annoying game. There is always something different happening. I do believe in order to catch "rare" or "cool" pokemon should be more of an option. It deffinitly is a game to get you outside, walking and moving while having fun. As someone who knows absolutely nothing about pokemon, I do enjoy this game and it definitely has the ability to continue growing to be better.

Great game if you have like 5 or 6 friends nearby to play with. Right now you don't even have to be close, just coordinate yourselves. It would be nice to communicate within the game tho. There's people i got on my friend list that i only know from there, and sometimes i would like to send a message like "raid in 10min" or something similar.

This one of my favorite games and I play it daily. But there is one problem I face a lot that is there is no option to message your PoGo friends which will make it really good as we can discuss and open gifts and ask for battles in the game itself. And one more is that there should be a option to put a mesaage at the time of raids also so that people can see that and join our lobby as sometimes many people are doing the raids and want to join the lobby and are not able to do.

Good Game, but has some issues which have taken me to write this review. First, the distribution of poke stops and gyms throughout the land is truly bad for those that live in villages or less crowded areas. I understand that makes more sense to have more where are more players, but try to spread some interesting spots each Km. Secondly, remove the limitation of 50 coins for the first day at a gym. Took over a gym in my village and haven't been able to neither get my pkmn back or get coins.

Oof. The reduced reach distance is really impacting the gameplay. We're supposed to avoid crowded spaces and yet at the same time get right on top of each pokestop? So many pokestops and gyms are in the middle of buildings or in private places, and are now yet again unreachable. My other complaint- outside of events, we get the same 10 pokemon appear in the wild and that's it. No more surprise of stumbling into something rare... I don't feel motivated to explore anymore when it's all the same.

It's much better than it was at launch, with a ton of things to do, trainers to battle, pokés to hatch. But you're screwed if you don't find a large, active community in your town. You NEED people for endgame content. Not only that, but there are still issues which Niantic won't address - like updating existing PokéStops/Gyms, adding new ones etc.

Basically it's like one of those pet collecting games but with AR and Pokémon. The game really only focuses on collecting Pokémon and trading them. There are some combat mechanics but it really leaves a lot to be wanted. There's not really much you can do with your Pokémon, trade or use them to fight which doesn't do much to them really. The game lacks a clear direction and just follows a more pokemon is better mentality without ever fixing gameplay mechanics or adding needed ones. Plus BUGS!

Downloaded this game in 2016 and played it all the time. After a while I uninstalled it as it didn't appeal to me as much. Yet here I am in 2021 writing a review. As you can probably already tell by this review I have reinstalled it recently and I must say, the game has not lost its touch. There are several new features and updates I never imagined would be part of Pokémon go and there are still so many things to do. Also my progress was not deleted despite a 4-5 year break. 5 stars 100%.

Great game. I love finding Pokémon, catching them and occasionally trying to beat a gym or raid. It's fun to play with my friends and we can trade, send gifts and even battle! However, it would be cool to add a feature where (if the player allows it) you can see if friends are online and maybe where they are so you can meet and play together. I think another good feature would be a messaging system so you can message friends who are online to ask to meet or trade etc.

Game is improving, as the "pay to win" feel at the same time. It will be interesting to see what happens next after the introduction of gen3. Battle, gyms and raiding system dynamics are incredibly simple and in desperate need of some depth. The weather influence was a good addition, but abilities will be needed at a certain point (i.e. soon). 95% of the pokemons are currently mere dex fillers with no actual use in the battle metagame.

Been playing since 2017 overall it's been a fun game to play. But more and more it feels like a pay to win. You can only really make the most out of the game if you have a very specific set of conditions. Gyms and pokestops near you, friends to play with and money to spare. Bugs are a minor problem aswell. From playing this game, you will find many advantages despite little disadvantages. Garbage, works purely on addiction factor and constant events trying to pull you in due to fear of missing something rare.
